header: /* The palette, type and spacing tokens. Dark is the default and primary
/* The breakpoint ladder. A custom property cannot be used in a media query, so
* this comment is the only place the ladder is written down — every
* `@media (max-width: …)` in these stylesheets picks a rung from it.
*   48rem  tablet portrait — also where `html` drops back to 100% (base.css)
*   56rem  the wide dialog stops holding two columns of form
*   70rem  the spending plan's rail and the dashboard's double-width widget
* Inside a media query a rem is always the browser's 16px — `html` at 125% does
* not reach here — so 48rem is 768px and 70rem is 1120px, whatever the page

comment: Surfaces, darkest to lightest. Depth is carried by these rather than by
shadows: a dense financial grid with a shadow on every card reads as noise.
Indigo is the brand and the interactive colour, and nothing else may be
indigo. `--accent` is a fill; indigo text reads `--accent-fg`. Every text
colour must reach 4.5:1 on every surface, hover included
(`contrast.test.ts`).
A glyph or a count on a saturated fill that is not the accent: a series
colour, the unread badge's coral. White in both themes.
Money has exactly two colours and they are never decorative: green is money
in, coral is money out or over budget. Anything else competing with them
makes a total unreadable at a glance.
Categorical chart series, ordered so that adjacent pairs stay
distinguishable — a legend of four must read before a legend of eight.
The Spending table's four shades, least to most spend: the accent at
rising strength, so the most-spent cell still carries body text.
For the things a `sm` corner would round away entirely: a 16px checkbox, an
8px legend swatch, the 3px marker on the ratio bar.
Fully round ends at any height: a pill, a dot, a bar's track.
Every single-line control — a button, an input, a select's trigger — is
this tall, so any two of them line up in a row.
A row of controls inside a card or a page header — the toolbar, a
card's or a header's actions, a table row's buttons — is this tall:
`btn--sm`, `search--sm` and a chip.
A table body row, and a register row, at each density: `Table density`
and the register's Customize Columns pick one, and the register's
virtualizer reads the same tokens (`ROW_HEIGHT_TOKENS`).
A table row with a second line (`Table lines={2}`): two lines of body
text and the same breathing room above and below as one.
Only what floats over the page casts a shadow, and the further above it,
the larger: a tooltip, then a menu or a toast, then a dialog.
A panel that slides over the page from one edge: the accounts drawer from
the left, a sheet from the bottom.
What dims the page under a dialog, and under a drawer that leaves the page
in view.
The shade a scroller casts over the content still behind its edge.
A focused or selected field's outline, drawn inside its own border so the
box does not grow.
A print is black on white whatever the screen's theme.
The stacking ladder, lowest first. What a layer covers must sit below it:
an open menu inside a dialog, a toast over everything. A component's own
0-2 for ordering its parts stays a literal.
A 4px scale at the root size.
Half a step, for the gap that holds two lines of one label together.
Between two cards, in a grid or a column, on every page.
The page's left and right edge, shared by the top bar so its title
starts where the page's content does.
The smallest box a finger can be asked to hit: a link in the phone's
sheet, a control that stands alone on a phone.
Icons by job: `sm` beside a line of text, `md` a control's glyph and a
row's leading icon, `lg` a tile's or an empty state's.
Wide enough for the longest destination's name. `--rail-width` is the one
that slides; this is where it slides to.
The rail's icon column, and the whole of the collapsed rail: every glyph
on the rail sits centred in a track this wide in both states, so
collapsing moves none of them.
How long anything takes to move. Every animated surface reads this, and
`MotionProvider` rewrites it on the root element from the display
preference; the number here is only the default before React runs.
0ms means no animation at all, so every rule that reads this must stay
correct at 0: an animation an unmount waits on is given 1ms at least,
so its end is still reported.
A state change a pointer causes under its own cursor. Derived, so
`MotionProvider`'s setting (zero included) reaches it too.
Amounts are tabular everywhere. A column of figures whose digits do not
line up cannot be scanned, and scanning is the only thing a register is for.
Seven sizes, each with a job: `xs` badges, eyebrows and in-bar
percentages; `sm` captions, hints and labels; `base` body text and h4;
`md` section and card headings (h2, h3); `lg` the page title and the
ceiling inside a page. Only the hero figures go past it:
2xl  the page's own total     — `.figure--total`
xl   a labelled stat in a row — `.figure--stat`
lg   the figure of one row or one small card — `.envelope__available`
Not a tier to size to by choice: for a digit that must fit a box smaller
than `xs` (the unread count, a chart's axis ticks).
Three weights: `regular` body, `medium` a control's label and a name in a
row, `semibold` a heading and a figure that is the point.
`tight` for a line that sits inside a fixed-height box (a badge, a
figure, a row's two lines); `body` for prose that wraps.
Both money colours darken in light mode: the dark-theme values fail
contrast on white, and an unreadable amount is worse than an ugly one.
The top bar's title is the first thing a wider gutter would cut.
Reduced motion wins over the preference. `MotionProvider` resolves the same
rule in JavaScript, because its inline `--motion` outranks any stylesheet;
this holds until it has run.
